privacy: All employee names, diagnoses, injury narratives, claim identifiers and medical details are excluded.
workflow_skeleton: record the reported/alleged work-related injury in the restricted case workflow
notify RTEC's current workers' compensation carrier/claims administrator within three working days of employer notification
separately evaluate current Kentucky OSH serious-incident reporting deadlines; fatality 8 hours and covered hospitalization/amputation/loss-of-eye 24 hours
carrier/administrator investigates and handles required FROI/SROI reporting to Kentucky
collect medical/work-status information through approved restricted channels
track lost time, restrictions and return-to-work status
coordinate payroll/leave/operations only on the minimum necessary work-status facts
historical_participants: medical provider documentation as case-specific evidence
controls_inferred_from_recurrence: Work status changes were not considered complete until external workers-comp follow-up occurred.
Return-to-work status was a recurring unresolved-commitment type suitable for structured tracking.
unresolved: Identify RTEC's current workers' compensation insurer, third-party administrator/claim administrator, policy/posting and reporting contact/portal
Identify current internal first-notification owner and backup owner
Confirm the RTEC internal incident/First Report form and whether IA-1 or a carrier-specific intake is used operationally
Document RTEC's current emergency, supervisor, safety, operations and HR escalation chain
Document current restricted medical/work-status storage and access controls
Document who makes Kentucky OSH serious-incident reports and how completion is evidenced
Document claim closure, OSHA log/reporting reconciliation and retention
guardrail: No historical case outcome or employee-specific fact is promoted as policy.

employer_obligations: Keep a record of workplace injuries received by employees.

Report any work-related injury, disease, or alleged work-related injury/disease to the workers' compensation carrier or party responsible for benefits within three working days of employer notification.

For an injury/disease causing more than one day away from work, the carrier/claims administrator is responsible for the First Report of Injury to the Department of Workers' Claims within one week after notification.

Maintain required workers' compensation coverage/posting; the current Kentucky employer guidance says the posting identifies the insurance company, policy information and how injured employees access medical care.
current_kentucky_baseline.state_claim_data_flow: Kentucky Department of Workers' Claims receives FROI/SROI electronically from carriers and third-party administrators through approved EDI vendors.

kentucky_osh_serious_incident_reporting.fatality: within 8 hours of employer awareness, subject to the current event/time-limitation rules
kentucky_osh_serious_incident_reporting.caution: Older Kentucky materials used a 72-hour rule for hospitalization/amputation/eye loss. Current Kentucky OSH guidance and 2025 update materials state 24 hours effective after the 2025 change.
